Confidence is medium because several dismissals rest on spec-sanctioned design intent rather than a full call-graph trace.

findings.title: Copilot delete classification has no test
findings.problem: regression-gap: callFileOperations classifies a path as 'delete' from toolTelemetry deletedPaths and from an apply_patch '*** Delete File:' header, but no test sends a deleted path. Every fixture passes deletedPaths '[]' and only Add/Update headers (grep of *.test.ts).
findings.impact: If the deleted.has(path) check or the Delete->'delete' mapping is dropped or inverted, deletions are reported as edits/writes and the filesDeleted counter (metrics-aggregator op.type === 'delete', metrics-sync-processor) undercounts Copilot deletions with no failing test.
findings.recommendation:
In copilot-cli.analytics.test.ts add a patchCall whose telemetry has deletedPaths: JSON.stringify([x]), and a second case with no telemetry and patch '*** Begin Patch
*** Delete File: x.txt
*** End Patch
'; assert parsed.metrics.fileOperations equals [{type:'delete', path:x}] in both.

findings.title: Run-scoped skill invocations are untested
findings.problem: regression-gap: skill.invoked is now counted only when inRun(event, bounds), but no bounded-run test contains a skill.invoked event; the only fixture with one is a whole-session parse in copilot-cli.parse.test.ts:40.
findings.impact: If the inRun guard on skills is dropped, a resumed Copilot run is credited with every skill invoked by earlier runs over the same native session (skill counts and session-source classification in parseSessionFile / parseCopilotRun), and the existing in-window tool/prompt tests still pass.
findings.recommendation: Add skill.invoked events to killResumeEvents inside run A's window and inside run C's window, then assert each bounded parseSessionFile (run A, and run C with startTime T0+900) counts only its own run's skill.

findings.title: Shutdown lines/files subtraction is untested
findings.problem: regression-gap: runShutdownShare subtracts the last shutdown before the run start from the last shutdown before run end for linesAdded/linesRemoved and filters prior filesModified, consumed by applyShutdownShare. No test has two shutdowns carrying codeChanges (one before, one inside a run); copilot-cli.analytics.test.ts:74 and :473 have a single shutdown each, and the runShutdownShare unit tests assert only premiumRequests.
findings.impact: If the subtraction or priorFiles filter regresses, a resumed Copilot run on a build without per-call line telemetry is credited again with every earlier run's lines and files, double-counting churn and breaking the EPMCDME-16474 'original session's numbers stay unchanged' guarantee, with no failing test. Consumer: parseSessionFile -> applyShutdownShare -> CopilotCliMetricsProcessor deltas.
findings.recommendation: In copilot-cli.analytics.test.ts ('runs over one resumed native session'): run A ends with a routine shutdown {codeChanges:{linesAdded:2, filesModified:[x]}} and no per-call line telemetry; run C resumes and its shutdown is {linesAdded:5, filesModified:[x,y]}. Assert run C's bounded parse yields fileOperations [{type:'edit', path:y, linesAdded:3, linesRemoved:0}].

findings.title: Sibling bound overrides nearer disk record bound
findings.problem: copilotRunWindows fetches on-disk next-record bounds only for runs with no loaded sibling, then builds bounds as new Map([...diskBounds, ...nextSiblingStart]), so a loaded sibling's start always wins. A record the report filtered out that started between this run and its next loaded sibling over the same native session is ignored, contradicting the function's own contract that 'the window does not depend on the report's filter'.
findings.impact: In a filtered analytics report (e.g. by project/branch) the run's window extends past the filtered-out run's start, so that run's tokens and cost are priced into this run, against EPMCDME-16474's 'tokens/cost come from the run's own requests'. Verified by reading the function and its single call site (cost-enricher.ts:584).
findings.recommendation: Fetch disk bounds for every copilot run with a start time (not only unbounded ones) and take the minimum of the loaded-sibling start and the on-disk next-record start per run, e.g. bounds.set(id, Math.min(sibling ?? Infinity, disk ?? Infinity)) with Infinity mapped back to undefined; add a cost-enricher test with a filtered-out record between two loaded siblings.
